## Decisions

- ⏳ **open** `l-archetype` `low confidence` (scaffold): Scaffolded as button (interactive: state axis has hover, focus, active; interactive, but nothing says which kind). Confirm, or re-run npm run specs:scaffold -- --slug=link --archetype=<link-card|card|collection>. _Evidence: decided by heuristic; token namespaces content×2, focus-ring×1; state axis default/hover/focus/active_
  - The draft chose: button — interactive: state axis has hover, focus, active; interactive, but nothing says which kind
  - Alternatives: link-card: A card that is one link: illustration or icon, a headline, optional description, an arrow affordance. The whole surface is the target and the headline is the accessible name.; card: A non-interactive content card; actions live in a slot.; collection: A row, grid or scroller of one repeated unit.; checkbox / radio: A selection control with a checked state, usually paired with a label.; toggle / switch: A binary on/off control that applies immediately.; input / field: Accepts typed input. Label, value, placeholder, and an error state.; badge / tag / chip: A small label. Non-interactive unless it is dismissible.; pagination: Moves between pages of content.; accordion: A disclosure: a trigger that shows and hides a region of content. Open or closed is a prop a consumer sets, not an interaction state.; select / dropdown: A choice among options. The native <select> does the choosing; the design styles the trigger around it.; helper text: Guidance or a message under a field: hint, error, success. Associated with its field, never floating.; list: A sequence of like items — features, links, steps. The items are the content; the list is the rhythm.
  - If wrong: npm run specs:scaffold -- --slug=link --archetype=<link-card|card|collection> --force

## Accessibility

WCAG 2.2 AA: `1.4.3`, `1.4.11`, `2.1.1`, `2.4.7`, `2.5.8`, `4.1.2`

- Renders a native <button>, or an <a> when it navigates — never a div with a click handler.
- The label is the accessible name; an icon-only button needs an aria-label.
- Focus is visible on the control itself (2.4.7) and the target is at least 24x24 (2.5.8).
- Disabled is conveyed to assistive tech, not by colour alone (1.4.1).
- Focus state shows a visible focus ring (WCAG 2.2 AA · SC 2.4.7 Focus Visible). Contrast holds in both themes because content/default resolves to a contrasting value per mode (SC 1.4.3 Contrast Minimum).
